title: Android <plurals>, and a Russian catalog rendering the wrong string today

census.why: XML routes to the markup extractor, which is what gives `<item quantity>` a structural path a dialect can read.
The translated catalog, whose locale comes from its DIRECTORY rather than from its name.

expectations.why: A form of a family, not a string on its own. Its verdict is the easy part; being grouped with its sibling is the point.
The second form. Together these two are one unit of work, and neither means anything alone.

A platform-native, machine-readable exception, and the catalog rule for this file says out loud that it must win over any heuristic. It did not: the file-level rule marked every string here translatable, so a URL somebody had deliberately fenced off came back `translate`. Checked before the rules now, and `hard`, so no agent verdict can undo it.
An ordinary resource string in the same file, so the case shows the rule working rather than only refusing.
Already Russian, and still found: `plurals` measures a catalog against ITS OWN locale, which needs the forms read whatever language they are in.

plurals.why: English selects two, and this has two. Complete. `code-edit` because adding an `<item quantity>` element is a markup edit, and the engine will not write XML it did not parse structurally.

The most valuable thing this whole tool produces. Russian selects four categories and this catalog has two, so the application renders the WRONG STRING for 2, 3 and 4 — today, in production, with nothing translated and no target language involved. The locale comes from the directory name, `values-ru`, which is Android's own convention and not a filename this tool invented.

knownGaps: `<string-array>` items are not read as a family and should not be — an array of weekday initials is calendar vocabulary, not a plural. They currently come back as ordinary translatable strings with no signal that reordering them breaks the calendar.
